description: Kills an app's process the way Android does to a backgrounded app that needs its memory, keeping its task and saved state: presses HOME if the app is on screen, waits until its activity is stopped (state saved), runs `am kill`, checks the process is gone, then (unless reopen: false) brings the task back like Recents does, so the activity that was on top is recreated from its saved state in a new process. Returns oldPid, newPid, killed, reopened, resumed (false: the activity did not come back, e.g. a crash while restoring; see get_crashes), and topActivity before and after. killed is false when the process survived (`am kill` spares a process with a foreground service or one another visible app uses). Unlike stop_app (a force-stop, which discards the saved state and the task). Killing the app being profiled ends its SDK link until it runs again. Device control.

reopen.description: Bring the task back afterwards (default true).

serial.description: adb serial; default: the session device, or the only ready one.

name: simulate_process_death
title: Simulate process death
